notes: The italicized 'be' is placed on basilei as the verbless clause's predicate: the nominatives time and doxa are the subject, so rule 63 keeps the copula off them, and rule 96 keeps it off the determiner-carrying article to, leaving the predicate noun to take it discontinuously under rule 15. The unit's note names the competing reading.
'the King eternal' leaves s004 unrepresented under rule 23, the ASV compressing ton aionon into the single adjective 'eternal' and writing no determiner there.
'the only God' follows rule 58's own worked example: mono stays bare and theo takes the supplied determiner.
The duration phrase follows rule 30 exactly: both articles unrepresented, 'ever' on the first aion and 'and ever' on the second, the juncture being a rule 29 helper.
